recommendation: Keep the fix as-is. It aligns active RDF source with the published Jira disposition and removes a conformance ambiguity for Bundle and multi-root RDF serializations.
issue_request: FHIR-18473 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core RDF issue asking why multiple tree roots were permitted after the RDF page said multiple roots meant the graph could not be parsed as a single resource. The approved resolution requires systems responding to a FHIR operation with a FHIR resource, including a FHIR Bundle, to have exactly one node marked as a tree root.
initial_application: The Jira comment reference GH#e2e131ac42 was not resolvable as a commit in the current checkout, but November 2018 xml-and-rdf history shows source/rdf.html already contained the multiple-treeRoot parse ambiguity sentence near the Jira vote/application period. Later RDF page changes preserved fhir:nodeRole/fhir:treeRoot but the current source no longer carried the explicit SHALL requirement.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml lists rdf.html as the active RDF Definition page under Resource Definitions. Later RDF usability issues FHIR-37937 through FHIR-37941 rewrote portions of the same page but did not supersede the one-treeRoot rule. The current paragraph also described the focal resource as the resource not contained in another resource, which is insufficient for Bundles because bundled entry resources are not contained resources.
reconciliation: Changed source/rdf.html to state that systems responding with a FHIR resource, including a FHIR Bundle, SHALL have exactly one node marked as fhir:treeRoot, and restored the deterministic consequence that multiple fhir:treeRoot nodes prevent parsing the Turtle statements as a single resource.
source_changes: source/rdf.html: clarified the focal-resource wording for contained or bundled resources and added the FHIR-18473 one-fhir:treeRoot SHALL requirement.
